rationale: Evidence from iteration 8 (score 690.4, best so far): the oval (20/20, about 1.86 s) and s-bend (20/20, about 2.06 s) are both solved. The slalom still fails 20/20 by off_track, but progress rose from 0.31 to 0.42 and line_loss_events fell to 0. The larger 16 mm sensor footprint therefore helped, and the line is no longer being lost. The remaining slalom failure is the robot drifting past the 0.06 m limit on fast alternating bends while still on the tape. Steering oscillation is low (0.16 oval, 0.27 slalom), so the robot is not jittering and has margin for more correction. Earlier, kp 3.0 with kd 1.1 gave only a small slalom gain (0.32 to 0.35), but that was with 12 mm sensors and a poorer signal. With the 16 mm footprint, the signal is smoother and stronger steering should now be more usable. Change: raise kp from 2.6 to 3.2 for more correction authority, and raise kd from 0.9 to 1.1 so damping keeps pace with the larger proportional term. Geometry, sensor weights, base_speed 0.85, ki 0 and last_direction line loss are unchanged, so the effect of the gain change is isolated. Expected result: slalom progress rises to about 0.45 to 0.55 with fewer off-track ends, and the oval and s-bend stay at or near 940 with no new oscillation. Hypotheses for the next race: (a) if slalom max_error stays near 0.063 with progress unchanged, steering gain is not the limit, so next I will test line_loss search_right or a lower base_speed of about 0.75 on the slalom; (b) if oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, kd must rise further with kp; (c) if the slalom now fails later but line_loss_events rise, the 16 mm footprint is overlapping background too much on tight bends and I will test 12 mm with the new gains. Measurements requested: all available measurements, so that per-track progress, max_error and oscillation can be compared with iteration 8.
